explanation.sentence: Profound hypotension and cold, clammy skin indicate shock, and the combination of low cardiac output and elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure points to cardiogenic shock.
Acute myocardial infarction (I) can reduce cardiac output by impairing ventricular contraction.
Rapid atrial fibrillation (II) can precipitate cardiogenic shock by shortening ventricular filling time and eliminating coordinated atrial contraction.
Severe valvular stenosis (IV) can limit forward flow; mitral stenosis, for example, can also elevate pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.
Hemorrhage typically causes hypovolemic shock, massive pulmonary embolism causes obstructive shock, and sepsis typically causes distributive shock.
